To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a field model of two component fermions is described which has consequences coinciding with the primary postulates of standard model, that such a model can be built for 4 generations minimum, and that analogues of Higgs fields appear naturally after transition to Grassmannian extra coordinate space.

(i) the standard model can be derived in its entirety as the low energy limit of a field theory with a composite fermion structure and (ii) the composite structure of the fundamental fermion field can be described by a field theory in a Grassmannian coordinate space.
the standard model of particle interactions is a consequence of the composite structure of the fermions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new interpretation of the standard model, in which it is assumed that the fundamental fermions of the theory are composite particles.
the problem of the composite nature for the fermions of the standard model.
a new approach to the problem of constructing the standard model, based on the assumption of composite nature of fundamental fermions and their fields.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the composite nature of fundamental fermions is the most natural explanation of the observed phenomena in the field of elementary particle physics.
the composite nature of quarks and leptons is the only possible basis for the construction of a realistic model of the fundamental interactions.

, in the context of the standard model, it is possible to construct a model of the fundamental fermion as a composite object, and that this model has a natural explanation for the existence of the generations and the Higgs field, and also explains the mechanism of the spontaneous symmetry breakdown and the origin of the masses of the gauge bosons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown how to construct the model of the standard model from first principles.
the composite nature of fermions and their internal structure is a necessary condition for the existence of the standard model.
the standard model is a model of composite fermions, and that the Higgs fields are composite objects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the standard model is a consequence of a field theory of composite fermions, where the composite nature is determined by the internal symmetry group of the fermion field.
the Higgs field can be a composite field.
the standard model can be considered as a model of two-component composite fermions.
